narrative.overview: The profile is a Solari split-flap departure board: a precise, mechanical instrument that flips and settles into place on load and reports what is moving today. Every visual is a physical object, a near-black flap board recessed in a graphite housing, and the same object hangs on GitHub's white page and its dark one, the way a real board is black in a sunlit hall and at midnight alike. The field is achromatic; colour is confined to one Solari amber (what is moving: velocity, today, the primary action) and to transit line bullets in each language's own colour. Density is that of signage, not of a dashboard: few rows, large flaps, printed condensed caps for labels, hairline rules between bands. Every glyph that matters sits on the flap cell lattice; the velocity number of a trending row is the row's largest element. Text is laid out from exact font advance widths, so right-alignment and truncation are measured, never guessed. The world was built for one hostile renderer. GitHub's sanitizer strips `style`, `class` and `script` from README HTML and splits ``, so every board is one theme-independent SVG inside a plain ``. This amends the original aluminium/graphite plan: the housing is a single graphite for both themes. Everything expressive (embedded fonts, keyframes, media queries) lives inside the SVG, where the sanitizer cannot reach. Confirmed rejections from the direction: no gradient-name capsule banner, no emoji, no skill-icon wall, no badge soup, no gradients, no glow. On yoshibase.com the same world, free of the README sanitizer, becomes a station hall. A hall ground one step darker than the board sits under everything; a full-width graphite board strip carries the monogram and a live UTC flap clock; the name and role are HTML split-flap cells; the profile painting hangs as a station poster in a graphite frame with a printed plaque; the outbound links are pale ticket stock dropped into a busker's open guitar case; a graphite notice plate carries the announcement; the footer ends on a "Mind the gap" platform stripe. Ticket stock is the one pale material in the hall. The case lining and a kraft cardboard sign are the only warm materials, and both are dark or muted enough that amber stays the only signal. The page is complete as static HTML: the build bakes the clock time, rebuild stamp, today's pick and barcodes, and JS only animates.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-independent near-black boards in one graphite housing, identical in light and dark GitHub themes.
Split-flap cells with two-tone halves, a hinge line and axle pins; a once-per-load flip cascade that settles.
One amber accent for motion and the primary action; language colour only as line bullets.
One signage family: Barlow Condensed for flaps and printed labels, Barlow for mixed-case descriptions.
Every asset generated nightly by Python stdlib, laid out from measured advance widths.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means moving or act-now: velocity, today, gain, activity, the primary action. Nothing static or decorative is amber beyond the board-title bullet, field labels and the monogram.

rules.name: The Object Rule
rules.body: Board colours never change with the GitHub theme. No light/dark pairs, no `<picture>`, no `prefers-color-scheme`.

rules.name: The Measured Text Rule
rules.body: All width-dependent layout (truncation, right-alignment, wrapping, legend spacing) uses the exact advances in `scripts/font_metrics.py`. Never estimate glyph widths; regenerate the table if a font file changes.

rules.name: The Flap Baseline Rule
rules.body: Flap glyphs centre on the hinge (baseline = cell height / 2 + font size x 0.35). Flap text is always uppercase; cells pad to the row's cell count with blank flaps.

rules.name: The Tertiary Layer Rule
rules.body: Anything not needed to read who, what, or how fast is wrapped in `t3` and must survive being hidden on phones.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No gradients, glows or coloured shadows. Depth is housing, recess and flap tone.

rules.name: The Hall Amber Rule
rules.body: On yoshibase.com, amber marks four things in the content: the clock colon, the primary (GitHub) ticket stub with its amber-ink barcode, the today dot on the live ticket, and the Mind-the-gap stripe. Beyond those, amber appears only in the inherited monogram and the interaction layer (focus ring, text selection). Secondary tickets stay on stock, and the case, the sign and the case props are never amber.

rules.name: The One Pale Material Rule
rules.body: Ticket stock is the only light surface in the hall, and it is reserved for the outbound destination tickets. Everything else sits on hall, board, graphite, lining or kraft.

rules.name: The Baked Page Rule
rules.body: `scripts/build_site.py` bakes every fact on the page: clock time, rebuild stamp, contribution line, today's pick and barcodes. JS only animates and keeps the clock current, so the page is complete with scripting off.

rules.name: The Shadow Carrier Rule
rules.body: A masked element cannot cast its own shadow. Its parent casts it with `filter: drop-shadow`, and the parent also draws the focus ring.

rules.name: The Hard-Stop Rule
rules.body: The No-Glow Rule bans visible colour gradients, not gradient syntax. Hard-stop gradients that draw flap halves, dashed route lines, the platform stripe and mask notches are drawing tools. Inner shading in a material's own deep tone (lining-deep on lining) is depth, not a coloured shadow.

dos: **Do** ship every board as one theme-independent SVG in a plain `` (inside `` when linked), with `width="100%"` on board rows.

**Do** keep contact-button lines in the `<a href="https://github.com` / `<a href="https://www.linkedin.com` line format; `scripts/commit_booster.py` matches them, and its badge regex relies on board rows carrying `width="100%"`.
**Do** emit the trending strip and its rows on one line so they share one HTML block and an even gutter.
**Do** embed fonts as base64 woff2 and keep all CSS inside the SVG.
**Do** keep the settled glyph visible by default and honour `prefers-reduced-motion` with the settled board.
**Do** wrap tertiary content in `t3` so the 600px media query can drop it.
**Do** keep the nightly pipeline Python stdlib only, laying out text with `scripts/font_metrics.py`.
**Do** bake every fact on yoshibase.com into the static HTML at build time; JS only animates and keeps the clock current.
**Do** cast a masked element's shadow and focus ring from its parent.
**Do** animate hall arrivals by transform only, and turn off flaps, drops, tilt and transitions under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** flip only the clock digits that changed.
**Do** keep faint ticket ink at 4.5:1 or better on both stock and stub shade.
donts: **Don't** use `<picture>`, `prefers-color-scheme`, or light/dark asset pairs; GitHub splits `<a><picture>`.
**Don't** put `style`, `class` or `script` in README HTML; the sanitizer strips them.
**Don't** use emoji or font glyphs as icons; flags render as two-letter origin codes and icons are authored SVG.
**Don't** use gradients, glow or coloured shadows.
**Don't** introduce a second accent; colour beyond amber appears only as line bullets.
**Don't** print anything except the outbound destination tickets on ticket stock.
**Don't** put amber on secondary tickets, the case, the sign or the case props.
